pages.text: "I'll ring the bell today!" Bami bounced below the cab's hanging bell rope. Dad smiled beside the big handle. The train could leave when the bell rang. Bami wanted the first ring today.
"Here goes!" Bami jumped and caught the rope in a foot. It wouldn't come down. Bami dangled, then dropped. "Why won't it work?"
Ten jumps, but the bell stayed silent. Bami sat on the floor. "I can't. The rope's too strong." Nabi lay curled in a corner and tapped Bami's foot with a tail.
Dad crouched beside Bami. "Everyone starts like that. I jumped twenty times when I was little." Bami sniffled. "If it doesn't work, pull again—until it does!"
Dad explained, "Don't just pull with your foot. Grip, then stretch your whole body down!" Nabi yawned and stretched. "Like that!" Bami tilted their head.
Bami jumped, gripped, and stretched down—but their foot slipped. Thump! This time, no tears. Bami looked at the rope. "It's okay. Try another pull!"
Second try! The rope came down a little, then stopped. The bell gave a tiny jingle. "A little better!" Dad stamped encouragement from the handle. "Try another pull!"
Third try! Grip tight, stretch all the way down—DING! Dad pulled the handle, and the train slowly started with a toot. Bami spread their wings. "I started it!"
The train rattled over a frozen-river bridge. Bami called to Dad, "One, it's okay if it doesn't work at first! Two, try another pull! Three, stretch until it works! Tomorrow, one jump and ding!"
Holding the big handle, Dad cuddled Bami with a wing. "What a fine conductor ringing the first bell!" Trying again brought progress little by little. Try another pull! Nabi waved a tail nearby.
